clue.text: Flat-foot having to tip a smaller amount!

parts.note: a ship that heels leans or tips over to one side
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A policeman is told he must hand over a smaller tip, with an exclamation of indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat-foot' looks like slang for a policeman, but it describes a foot that rests flat because the shoe lacks a raised back.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a raised back to the shoe, the wearer's foot sits flat on the ground.

parts.note: pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious
NE is north-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A preacher's self-righteous instructions go on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn or ache for something, as to long does.

indicators.note: a manufacturer makes things, so the letters of the word drawer are made into something new

parts.note: the fodder for the rearrangement; that it also spells the answer backwards is a coincidence of the setter's choice

explanation.surface: An award goes to a firm that builds chests of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or bounty given for good work acknowledges merit.

clue.text: Display expertise in building flying machines

parts.note: to air something is to show it off or display it
craft means skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Engineers show off their skill constructing planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in building' simply joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes, helicopters and gliders are all machines built to fly; the word is the same in singular and plural.

parts.note: reads as a regrettable result of a mistake, but means the feeling of being sorry that follows wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A mistake has an unfortunate result.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse and repentance are what a person feels after doing wrong.

indicators.note: something behaving erratically moves unpredictably, so the letters of meteor are jumbled

explanation.surface: A far-off shooting star wanders off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away or far off in space, like a remote island.

parts.note: reads as a payment having been made, but describes matter that has sunk to the bottom of a liquid

explanation.surface: Someone confirms the down payment has been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt or dregs are the matter that sinks and collects at the bottom of a liquid.

clue.text: Reflected it was no longer properly organised

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reverses things, so the word it is turned round

parts.note: something that died no longer exists

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the place used to be tidy but isn't any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Put neatly in order, as a room is after being cleaned up.

parts.note: sounds like dealing with urgent matters, but literally means doing the work of pressing clothes

explanation.surface: An executive handled urgent matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot iron is the job of pressing them.

clue.text: Spend lavishly, being in low spirits

definitions.meaning: to ... money is British slang for squandering it

explanation.definitionFit: Squandering money is an old British slang sense of the verb; feeling sad or down is the common adjective sense.

parts.note: reads as a grand denial, but means a monarch giving up the throne

explanation.surface: A grand statement denying responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: When a king or queen renounces the throne, Majesty is formally disclaimed.

indicators.note: breaking a horse tames it, and here the letters of a steed are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider grew anxious while training a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Teased in the sense of pestered or harassed, as a dog worries a bone.

clue.text: Inform about a mad character going to pieces

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it, so sing goes round the mad character

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland, a famous crazed character

explanation.surface: Someone reports on a lunatic who is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into fragments, as glass does when smashed.

parts.note: ex means former, so once or at one time
a pitman works down a coal pit, a miner

explanation.surface: A tester who used to be a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is TESTER, the 19-down answer; an inspector who checks work is both.
explanation.definitionFit: One who checks and assesses is an inspector or tester.

clue.text: The way some music can result in flight

parts.note: ST abbreviates street, a way
airs are tunes, some music

explanation.surface: The right melodies can make you want to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like escape, but a flight is a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a continuous set of steps between floors.

indicators.note: the situation word goes inside the reversed synonym of cut
placed after cut, back means that word's synonym is read the other way, giving REVES

parts.note: to sever is to cut
the lie of the land is how things are situated

explanation.surface: A remedy eases the position during a period of cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' reads as a spending cut, but splits into a synonym of cut plus a reversal signal; 'the situation' is the lie, as in the lie of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Eases or lessens pain or distress.

clue.text: Not all restrictions are exactly observed

indicators.note: only part of the word restrictions is used, so the answer lies within it

explanation.surface: Some rules are not followed to the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules that are rigorously and precisely kept are rigid ones.

definitions.meaning: one who covers roofs with reeds

explanation.definitionFit: A roofer who covers buildings with reeds or straw, and the surname of Britain's first woman prime minister.

indicators.note: repairing remakes something, so the letters of street are reassembled

explanation.surface: An inspector in charge of mending roads.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner checks and tests things, as an inspector does.

clue.text: Having done badly, the egghead is really sweet

parts.note: past means over or finished, having been done
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: After a poor performance, the intellectual is truly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like a brainy person, but splits into 'egg' and 'head': the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge or small medicated sweet, such as a fruit gum.

clue.text: Some men dread her emotional hold

indicators.note: only some of the letters of men dread her emotional are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some men fear an emotional woman's grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick fast or cling, as glue holds.

clue.text: Imprisoned these days for a five year stretch

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Jailed nowadays for a five-year sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' looks like a prison term, but means a period of five years or a group of five.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group or period of five, here five years.

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
MA, Master of Arts, a scholar's degree

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an academic's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a brimmed straw hat.

clue.text: An American place for 25 maybe — maybe not

definitions.text: An American place for 25 maybe — maybe not

parts.words: An American place for 25 maybe — maybe not
parts.note: a US city named after a royal Charles, who was a prince at one time but a king when it was named

explanation.surface: A US town perhaps named for a prince, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is PRINCE. The South Carolina city was named for King Charles II, so 'maybe not' a prince; the name is also that of a 1920s dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in South Carolina named after the English king Charles II.

clue.text: People must get the right one

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Everyone must pick the correct one.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a people or nation sharing descent.

definitions.meaning: a level or grade in a hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means gross or foul; as a noun it is a position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Pole in charge — a man of high rank

indicators.note: the pole letter goes in the word for charge

parts.note: a price is what one charges
N, the north pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man in command is a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but is N for north pole, placed inside PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal son ranks just below the monarch.

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or unreal, so the letters of Cameron's are rearranged

explanation.surface: David Cameron tells tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Romances are tales of love or adventure.
